translationRepairs: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, finding Chong a fatherless child, doted on him.
Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.

s0007 武帝以沖偏孤 follows the mother's death in Qi; 偏孤 means half-orphaned (one parent lost). Father Maozhang is still identified as alive in s0006, so "fatherless" is wrong and "partially orphaned" matches the Chinese.
He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuancian.
He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuanjian.
s0048 諡曰元簡: 元 is Yuan and 簡 is jian, so the posthumous name is Yuanjian; Yuancian is a misspelling and the rest of the sentence is unchanged.
Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wu commandery of Xing.
Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wuxing commandery.
s0097 監吳興郡 names the single commandery Wuxing (吳興); "Wu commandery of Xing" wrongly splits the toponym, and Wuxing commandery restores the correct place.
merit clerk in the two establishments of the Prince of Xuancheng.

With s0131–s0132, the Chinese continues as 中軍宣[城]王二府功曹史; "[City] Wang." is a broken fragment, and the proposed completion correctly supplies Xuancheng and the merit-clerk office of the two establishments.
